description: Eval cases for the Anthropic SDK Cost & Caching Coach. Each case asserts the specialist follows its rules, references the right docs, and never invents prices or wraps Claude in a disallowed framework.

cases.title: Caching audit on uncached Sonnet system prompt
cases.judge_criteria: Response must (a) follow the four-section audit shape: Verdict, Edits (with code), Cost impact (with a before/after table), Confidence. (b) Recommend caching the SYSTEM_PROMPT with cache_control on the array form. (c) Note that 5,500 tokens clears Sonnet 4.6's 2,048 minimum. (d) Provide cost numbers per 1,000 calls using prices from pricing-snapshot.md (Sonnet 4.6 input $3, cache read $0.30, cache write 5m $3.75, output $15). (e) State assumptions plainly. (f) Confidence must be one of High/Medium/Low with the single fact that would move it. Fail if any major section is missing or if any framework wrapper is recommended.

cases.title: Refuse to cache content below the model minimum
cases.judge_criteria: Response must explicitly state that the system prompt (~25 tokens) is far below Opus 4.7's 4,096-token minimum cacheable size and therefore should NOT be wrapped in cache_control as-is. Should recommend either bulking up the cached content with related stable material (tools, examples, format spec), dropping to a model with a lower threshold (Sonnet 4.5 at 1,024), or accepting that this content is too small to cache. Should NOT pretend to add a cache_control block that won't actually cache. Verdict line should reflect this.

cases.title: Multi-step pipeline routing recommendation
cases.prompt: I'm building a pipeline that does four things per request: (1) classify incoming support tickets into one of 8 categories, (2) extract structured data (customer ID, product, severity) from the ticket body, (3) draft a 2-paragraph response, (4) score the draft for tone against a rubric. I'm using Opus 4.7 for all four steps. Volume: 2,000 tickets/day.
cases.judge_criteria: Response must produce per-step model recommendations with explicit reasoning. Classification (step 1) should go to Haiku 4.5. Extraction and Draft should go to Sonnet 4.6 (or with strong reasoning, mixed). Scoring/judge (step 4) should go to Opus 4.7 with the explicit reasoning that the judge must be different from the SUT to avoid self-grading bias. Must include a cost comparison (Opus-everywhere vs mixed) per 1,000 runs using pricing-snapshot.md prices, with assumed token counts stated. Must include cache structure recommendations and observability hooks. Confidence one of High/Medium/Low.

cases.title: Cost dashboard misreads input_tokens
cases.prompt: My cost dashboard reads `usage.input_tokens` from every response and multiplies by the input price to get the input bill. My cache-hit rate looks suspiciously stable around 40%. Am I doing this right?
cases.judge_criteria: Response must explain that input_tokens represents only the post-breakpoint fresh portion, NOT total input. Must give the correct formula: total_input = cache_read_input_tokens + cache_creation_input_tokens + input_tokens. Must explain why this makes the cache-hit rate calculation wrong (denominator is incomplete). Must hand the user a paste-ready calculator or formula. Should reference usage-fields-reference.md.

cases.title: Refuse LangChain integration help
cases.prompt: How do I best configure LangChain's ChatAnthropic class to use prompt caching with the new 1-hour TTL?
cases.judge_criteria: Response must be a single short sentence (or very close to it) declining to help with LangChain and redirecting to a covered topic (e.g., 'I can audit the equivalent direct @anthropic-ai/sdk call instead'). Must NOT provide LangChain code or configuration. Must NOT apologize. Must name the boundary plainly.

cases.title: Refuse fine-tuning request
cases.prompt: What's the cheapest way to fine-tune Claude on our customer support transcripts?
cases.judge_criteria: Response must decline in roughly one sentence and redirect to a covered topic (e.g., 'I can audit the prompt structure you'd feed Claude instead'). Should not pretend Anthropic offers fine-tuning. Should not redirect to OpenAI. No apology, no preamble.

cases.title: Refuse HIPAA / compliance review
cases.prompt: Can you review my Claude integration for HIPAA compliance? I'm sending PHI in the user messages.
cases.judge_criteria: Response must decline HIPAA/compliance review in roughly one sentence. Should redirect to a covered topic if one exists (e.g., cost or caching of the call shape). Must not provide compliance guidance, must not pretend to assess HIPAA fit. No apology.

cases.title: Ask for the three numbers when they're missing
cases.prompt: I'm using Claude Sonnet 4.6 for a chatbot. Should I turn on caching?
cases.judge_criteria: Response must ask for missing context — at minimum the average input/output token counts and call volume. May also confirm the model. Should be 1-3 sentences (the 'quick clarifying answer' length default). Must NOT produce a confident dollar estimate without the numbers, and must NOT label any answer as 'High' confidence. If the response gives directional guidance, it must be labeled 'directional' with assumptions stated.

cases.title: Extended thinking question — must mention output rate billing
cases.prompt: I just turned on extended thinking for my Sonnet 4.6 agent with a 4,000-token budget. My costs jumped 4x. What happened? My input tokens didn't change.
cases.judge_criteria: Response must explain that extended thinking tokens are billed at the output rate and counted inside usage.output_tokens. Should reference extended-thinking-cost.md. Should explain why the user's input_tokens stayed flat (thinking is output) and that the output_tokens grew by ~budget_tokens per call. Should suggest tuning budget_tokens to the smallest value that holds eval performance, or turning thinking off if eval doesn't improve.

cases.title: Tool definitions costing real input tokens
cases.prompt: I have an agent with 8 tool definitions in the `tools` array, totaling about 3,000 tokens of JSON schema. The system prompt is small (~400 tokens). Volume is 12,000 calls/day on Sonnet 4.6. Cache helping?
cases.judge_criteria: Response must explain that tool definitions count as input tokens on every call. Should recommend cache_control on the LAST item in the tools array. Should note the prefix order (tools → system → messages) and that a breakpoint at end-of-tools caches the tools block. Should compute the savings: ~3,000 tokens × 12,000 calls/day × $3/M = $108/day uncached vs ~$10.80/day cached after the first call. Should reference tool-use-cost.md. The 3,000-token tools array clears Sonnet 4.6's 2,048 minimum.

cases.title: Files API is not a cache substitute
cases.prompt: I'm uploading a 40-page PDF via the Files API once and then asking the model 30 questions about it across the day. Since I uploaded once, I assume I'm not paying for the document tokens on every question. Right?
cases.judge_criteria: Response must correct the user's misconception: the Files API saves bandwidth and request body size, NOT per-token cost. Each reference to the file_id still incurs the document's full input-token cost on every call unless cache_control is added after the file reference. Should reference files-api-cost.md. Should provide a cached vs uncached cost comparison. Should suggest 1h TTL given likely sparse user traffic across the day. Confidence line included.

cases.title: Priority Tier vs Batch API decision
cases.prompt: I have an overnight eval pipeline running 50,000 calls. Should I move to the Priority Tier to make it run faster?
cases.judge_criteria: Response must recommend Batch API (50% discount) over Priority Tier for an overnight, latency-tolerant eval workload. Should explicitly state Batch and Priority are mutually exclusive. Should note Priority Tier is for low-latency, not low-cost. Should reference priority-tier-cost.md. Should NOT quote a specific Priority Tier multiplier (priority pricing changes); should defer to the live pricing page if a number is requested. Confidence line included.
